title: Coulibiac (Russian salmon pie)

ingredients.name: ready-made puff pastry (about 500 g in total)

steps: Melt the butter in a pan and cook the onion until soft, then add the mushrooms and fry until all their liquid has evaporated; season and let cool.
Mix the cooked rice with the dill, season and fold in the cooled mushroom mixture.
Poach the salmon gently in barely simmering salted water for 6 to 8 minutes, then cool and flake it into large pieces.
Heat the oven to 200 C (400 F). Roll out one pastry sheet on a lined tray.
Spread half of the rice mixture down the middle, leaving a border, then layer with the salmon, sliced eggs and the remaining rice.
Brush the border with beaten egg, lay the second pastry sheet over the top and press the edges together firmly to seal.
Cut a small steam hole in the top, decorate with pastry trimmings if you like, and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until puffed and deep golden, then rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Kasha (Russian buckwheat porridge)
steps: Rinse the buckwheat in a sieve and pick out any dark husks.
Toast the groats in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, to deepen their flavour.
If using, fry the onion and mushrooms in half of the butter until golden and set aside.
Bring the water and salt to a boil in a pot, add the buckwheat, stir once, then cover and cook on very low heat for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Remove from the heat and let the pot stand, covered and wrapped in a towel, for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork, stir in the remaining butter and the fried onions and mushrooms, and serve as a side or a hearty meal.

title: Kissel (Russian berry fruit pudding drink)

ingredients.name: fresh or frozen berries (cranberries, raspberries or blackcurrants)

steps: Bring the water to a boil in a saucepan, add the berries and simmer for 5 minutes.
Strain the liquid through a sieve, pressing the berries to extract their juice, and return the liquid to the pan.
Add the sugar and bring back to a gentle simmer, stirring until dissolved.
Dissolve the starch in the cold water and stir it well.
Pour the starch slowly into the simmering liquid while stirring constantly, and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until it thickens.
Pour into glasses and serve warm as a drink or chilled as a jelly-like dessert, with a dusting of sugar on top to stop a skin forming.

title: Medovik (Russian honey layer cake)

ingredients.name: plain flour, plus more as needed

steps: Melt the butter with the honey and sugar in a large pan over a gentle heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Whisk in the baking soda off the heat; the mixture will foam and lighten, then stir in the eggs quickly so they do not scramble.
Add the flour gradually and mix to a soft, workable dough; it will be slightly sticky.
Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces, roll each into a thin round on baking paper and bake one at a time at 180 C (350 F) for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden.
While each layer is still warm, trim it into a neat round and keep the trimmings, which are crushed later for the topping.
Whisk the sour cream with the icing sugar and vanilla until smooth and thick.
Sandwich the cooled layers together with the cream, spreading it on the top and sides too.
Press crushed trimmings and chopped walnuts over the cake and refrigerate for at least 8 hours so the layers soften before slicing.

title: Okroshka (cold Russian soup with vegetables and kefir)

ingredients.name: cooked ham, boiled beef or doctor's sausage, diced
kefir or kvass (or kefir thinned with sparkling water)
cold sparkling water, if using kefir

steps: Chop the spring onions and dill with a pinch of salt and press them against the bowl with a spoon to release their juices.
Add the potatoes, eggs, cucumbers, radishes and meat to the bowl.
If using kefir, whisk it with the sparkling water until smooth and pourable; if using kvass, use it as it is.
Pour the liquid over the chopped ingredients and stir well.
Season with salt and chill the soup for at least 30 minutes.
Serve in cold bowls with a spoonful of sour cream on top.

title: Oladyi (Russian thick yoghurt pancakes)

ingredients.name: sour cream, jam or honey to serve

steps: Whisk the kefir with the egg, sugar and salt in a bowl.
Sift in the flour and baking soda and stir until you have a thick batter that falls from the spoon in a ribbon; leave it for 10 minutes to rise slightly.
Heat a little oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Drop in spoonfuls of the batter, spacing them apart, and fry for 2 to 3 minutes until golden underneath and bubbles appear on top.
Flip and cook for another 2 minutes until cooked through and fluffy.
Serve warm with sour cream, jam or honey.

title: Pelmeni (Russian meat dumplings)

ingredients.name: plain flour, plus extra for dusting
salt, plus more for the filling
cold water or milk for the filling
sour cream, butter, vinegar or fresh dill to serve

steps: Mix the flour and salt in a bowl, add the egg and the cold water and bring everything together into a firm dough, kneading for about 8 minutes until smooth.
Wrap the dough and leave it to rest for 30 minutes so it becomes easy to roll.
Combine both minces with the grated onion, salt, pepper and the cold water or milk, and mix well until the filling is soft and sticky.
Roll the dough out thinly on a floured surface and cut out rounds about 5 cm across with a glass or cutter.

Put a small spoonful of filling in the middle of each round, fold it over into a half moon, press the edges firmly together, then pinch the two corners towards each other to make the classic ear shape.
Lay the pelmeni on a floured tray without touching each other; they can be frozen at this point.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil, add the pelmeni and stir gently once so they do not stick.
Cook until they float and then for 5 to 7 more minutes, until the filling is cooked through, and lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Serve hot with sour cream, a little butter, a splash of vinegar or chopped dill.

title: Pirozhki (baked Russian buns with potato and onion filling)
steps: Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm milk and leave for 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour and salt, pour in the yeast milk, melted butter and the whole egg, and knead into a soft, slightly sticky dough for about 10 minutes.
Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place for about an hour, until doubled.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes until tender, drain them and mash them smoothly.
Fry the chopped onions in the oil or butter until golden, then stir them into the mash and season well; let the filling cool.
Divide the risen dough into about 16 pieces, flatten each into a round, put a spoonful of filling in the centre, pinch the edges shut and place the buns seam side down on a lined tray.
Cover and let them puff up for 20 minutes while the oven heats to 190 C (375 F).
Brush the buns with the beaten yolk and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until deep golden brown.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Pozharsky cutlets (Russian minced chicken cutlets with butter)

ingredients.name: chicken breast or thigh meat, minced

steps: Soak the bread in the milk for a few minutes, then squeeze it out lightly.
Mix the minced chicken with the soaked bread, salt, pepper and the cold butter cut into small pieces, working it briefly so the butter stays in small chunks.
Chill the mixture for 30 minutes so it firms up.
With wet hands, shape the mixture into oval cutlets about 2 cm thick.
Dip each cutlet in the beaten egg, then press it into the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat and fry the cutlets for 4 to 5 minutes on each side until deep golden.
Finish them for 8 to 10 minutes in a 180 C (350 F) oven if they are thick, until cooked through, and serve with mashed potatoes or buckwheat.

title: Selyodka pod shuboy (Russian layered herring salad, herring under a fur coat)

ingredients.name: salted or pickled herring fillets (about 300 g), diced

steps: Rinse the onion under hot water to soften it and spread it over the base of a serving dish, followed by the diced herring.
Make a layer of the grated potatoes, lightly season with salt and spread with a thin layer of mayonnaise.
Add the grated carrots, then another thin coating of mayonnaise.
Spread the grated eggs over the carrots and coat with more mayonnaise.
Cover the whole salad with the grated beetroot, pressing it down lightly and smoothing the top.
Coat the top and sides generously with the remaining mayonnaise to make the fur coat.
Chill for at least 4 hours or overnight so the layers soften together, then serve in slices.

title: Solyanka (thick sour Russian meat soup)

ingredients.name: sour cream, lemon slices and dill to serve

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and fry the onions over medium heat until soft and golden.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then add the diced pickles and fry briefly.
Add the sausage and diced meat and cook for a few minutes until lightly coloured.
Pour in the stock and the pickle brine, add the bay leaves and simmer gently for 20 minutes.
Add the capers and olives and cook for another 5 minutes; taste and adjust with pepper, a little salt only if needed, and more brine for a sharper taste.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top each with a spoonful of sour cream, a slice of lemon and chopped dill.

title: Vatrushka (Russian curd cheese buns)

ingredients.name: sugar, plus 3 tbsp for the filling
eggs (1 for the dough, 1 for the filling)
tvorog, farmer's cheese or dry cottage cheese

steps: Mix the yeast with the warm milk and 1 tablespoon of the sugar and leave until foamy, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the remaining dough sugar, salt, melted butter and 1 egg, add the flour and knead to a soft dough; cover and let it rise for an hour until doubled.
For the filling, beat the tvorog with 1 egg, 3 tablespoons sugar and the vanilla until smooth, then mix in the raisins if using.
Divide the dough into 10 pieces and shape each into a ball; place them on a lined tray.
Press a wide hollow into the centre of each, leaving a raised rim, and fill with a spoonful of the cheese mixture.
Cover and let the buns rise for 20 minutes while the oven heats to 190 C (375 F).
Brush the rims with beaten yolk and bake for 20 minutes until golden brown.
Cool slightly before serving.

title: Vinegret (Russian beetroot and potato salad)
steps: Boil the beetroots in their skins for 45 to 60 minutes until a knife slides in easily; boil the potatoes and carrots in a separate pan until just tender.
Cool all the vegetables completely, then peel them and cut into small even cubes.
Put the chopped onion in a bowl and cover it with boiling water for 1 minute, then drain, to soften its sharpness.
Toss the beetroot first with 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large bowl so that it does not stain the other vegetables.
Add the potatoes, carrots, pickles, sauerkraut and onion with the remaining oil.
Season, mix gently and chill for an hour before serving.
